title: Select Theme Class
prompt: A React layout component receives a theme prop. Write a helper that returns "theme-dark" for dark mode, "theme-light" for light mode, and "theme-system" when no theme is provided.

explanation.beginner:
Example: selectThemeClass("dark") produces "theme-dark". Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Compare “returns light class”: input ["light"] produces "theme-light". Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Tempting mistake: Capitalization, whitespace, and boolean-versus-string output are part of the contract; truthiness alone may combine distinct states.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “returns light class”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
